pages.name: Using Drugs
pages.html:
Drugs

Drugs: Spacers can purchase different pharmaceutical drugs for a variety of purposes, including to aid them as needed.

  • Dosage: Prices are given for 1 dosage.
  • Synergy: Multiple drugs can be taken for multiple effects to take place simultaneously. Any drawbacks are also incorporated into the effects, but multiply the drawback by D3.
  • Legality: On many worlds drugs are illegal, so to determine if a certain drug that characters are looking for is legal, roll OVER the local Law Level. Medical drugs are not affected by this, unless in an Amber Zone or Red Zone.
  • Availability: To determine if a drug can be readily found, roll the necessary roll under the drug’s Available chance, but apply a DM equal to the difference between the drug’s Tech Level and the planet’s Tech Level. For example, on a planet with TL11, gain a +2DM when looking for Combat drugs (TL9), while if on a TL7 world, then the spacers would incur a -2DM when looking for Combat drugs.
  • Addiction: A referee can choose to have characters experience drawbacks from over-consuming drugs.
    • Chance for addiction; A character can prevent becoming dependent on the drug if they only consume it once every week for Slow, Combat, PSI, and Recreational drugs or once every three months for Fast drugs. Consuming a drug within the abuse window requires the character to make an END roll equal to or more than the drug’s Available roll to avoid dependency.
    • Effect of addiction: A character gains a -D3 penalty to END every week they don’t consume the drug. If END reaches 0, then they take damage to their STR and DEX equally. If they do consume the drug during this period, they automatically recover 3 wounds.
    • Treatment: Addiction can be treated with a one-month medical stay at a treatment center on a TL12 planet, for 50,000Cr.

Book p.120

pages.name: Drug Descriptions
pages.html:
Drug Descriptions

  • Slow: Users experience time at a slower rate by accelerating their metabolism, allowing them to act twice as much in a combat round. The drug takes 1 minute to take effect and lasts for 10 minutes. The spacer takes 1D damage after the drug wears off and is “pinned” for a number of 10 minute intervals equal to the damage taken.
  • Slow (Medical): The user is medically placed in an unconscious state for 30 hours and recovers from injuries or illness as if 30 days have passed.
  • Slow (Antidote): Cancels the effect of a Slow drug, but the subject still suffers any ill effects from the Slow drug.
  • Fast: Users experience time at a much faster rate, so that they perceive 1 minute as 1 hour of time. The user is extremely vulnerable to harm due to their 60-to-1 ratio of time, and they often need assistance. This is used by wealthy people to slow aging and prevent boredom during long stretches of time, such as in jump-space.
  • Fast (Antidote): Cancels the effect of a Fast drug, but the subject still suffers any ill effects from the Fast drug.
  • Anagathic: Halts the aging process. Used to prevent aging both for vanity and to avoid any decline of physical capabilities. One dose lasts for 30 days.
  • Truth: Used to force someone to speak truthfully for one minute. They can resist the effects with a 8+ END check for every question asked, with a -1DM if a prior question was asked. Only six questions can be asked in the minute, or at a rate of one per combat round. After the one-minute time frame passes, the subject is rendered unconscious for one hour and incurs 2D damage from the drug.
  • Medical: Used to describe any drug that can aid in healing or recovery. The referee can use this to provide drugs for curing an illness, healing wounds, as an antidote to poisoning, to remove radiation, etc. Must be administered by someone with a rank in a Medical Skill, with a roll of an 8+. A failed administration of the drug wastes it without effect.
  • PSI-Drug: Allows a psionic character a way to temporarily enhance their psionic abilities. PSI drugs can only be found when interacting with an associate of a psionic institute, and they have a 8+ chance of having access to the drugs and the desire to sell them.
    • Boost: Gain +3 PSI to use immediately for up to one hour of time.
    • Double: Gain +6 PSI to use immediately for up to one hour of time.
    • Special: Gain +1 PSI per hour, allowing the psionic character to accumulate up to 15 PSI maximum over the course of 15 hours.
  • Recreational: This represents any drug that provides a non-utility alteration of the metabolism or mind to get high, relax, or hallucinate. Recreational drugs are normally illegal in most parts on any world, requiring a roll of 9+ to determine if they are legal. These drugs can be found using the Availability chance. The referee can choose what the drugs are and how they affect someone who takes them.

Book p.120
